findings.title: Credential from user storage is removed via local removeStoredCredentialById()
findings.body: `isRecoveryAuthnCodeInputValid()` now obtains the credential through `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential()`, which may return a credential that comes from the external user storage (`getFederatedCredentialsStream()`), not from the local/federated credential store. When all codes are used the code still calls `authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())`. For a credential returned by a user-storage provider the id is not a local credential id, and providers that build the model with `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(...)` (as the new `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials()` does) do not set an id at all, so `getId()` is `null`. Calling `removeStoredCredentialById(null)` on the JPA store performs an `em.find()` with a null primary key, which throws `IllegalArgumentException`, turning the last successful recovery-code login into a server error; at best it is a silent no-op and the exhausted codes are never removed from the user storage. The removal must be skipped (or delegated to the provider) when the credential originates from user storage.

findings.title: Existing local recovery-codes credential is not removed when codes are stored in user storage
findings.body: `createRecoveryCodesCredential()` writes the new codes to the user storage when `updateCredential()` returns true and in that case does nothing with any recovery-codes credential already present in the local (federated) credential store. `UserCredentialManager.isValid()` consults both the user storage and the local providers, so a previously stored local set of recovery codes stays valid indefinitely after the user regenerates codes (e.g. after the user-storage provider gained recovery-code support, or after the required action is re-run). The user believes the old codes were replaced while they can still be used to authenticate. The local credential of type `recovery-authn-codes` should be deleted when the codes are successfully stored in the user storage.

findings.title: Undocumented credential-input format for recovery codes; user label and generatedAt are dropped
findings.body: The code passes the generated codes to the user storage as a JSON array of plaintext codes in the `UserCredentialModel` value, while validation later passes a *single* raw code (`UserCredentialModel.buildFromBackupAuthnCode`) with the same credential type. Third-party `CredentialInputUpdater`/`CredentialInputValidator` implementations therefore have to distinguish between two completely different payload formats for the same credential type, and nothing in the SPI or javadoc documents this contract. In addition, the user-supplied label and the `generatedAt` timestamp that are present in `credentialModel` are not transmitted at all, so a provider cannot store them (the account console will show no label and a provider-invented creation date). Either send the full `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` data or document the expected format explicitly.

findings.title: NPE in getCredentials() when the user is not present in the in-memory map
findings.body: `getCredentials()` dereferences the result of `getMyUser(user)` (`myUser.recoveryCodes`, `myUser.otp`) without a null check, unlike every other method in this class (`getDisableableCredentialTypesStream`, `isConfiguredFor`, `isValid` all guard for `myUser == null`). The backing map lives only in the factory's memory, so after a server restart (or if the federated link survives removal from the map) `getMyUser()` returns null and any call going through `SubjectCredentialManager.getFederatedCredentialsStream()` – which is now on the login path via `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential()` – fails with a NullPointerException instead of returning an empty stream.

findings.title: Test does not cover one-time use / rotation / exhaustion of user-storage recovery codes
findings.body: `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin` only sets the codes up and logs in once with code #0 (`enterRecoveryCodes(..., 0, recoveryKeys)`). The stub provider's `isValid()` (BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage, ~line 340) just checks list membership and never marks a code as used, and `getCredentials()` rebuilds the credential from the complete list on every call, so `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean` will always request code #0 and the very same code can be replayed forever. Nothing in the test asserts that a code cannot be reused, that the next login asks for the next code, or that the exhaustion path (`allCodesUsed()` -> credential removal + `CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES` required action) works for credentials held in user storage. As written the test would pass even if one-time-use semantics are completely broken for user-storage-backed recovery codes.

findings.title: Recovery codes stored in user storage cannot be disabled/removed
findings.body: `disableCredentialType()` and `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream()` were not extended for `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE`, although `updateCredential()`/`isConfiguredFor()`/`isValid()` now support it. Consequently once recovery codes are written into this provider they can never be removed through the admin or account APIs, and the exhaustion path in `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator` has no way to clear them. Since this provider is the reference implementation exercised by the new test, the removal/disable side of the feature is both unimplemented and untested.

findings.title: getCredentials() also exposes the OTP credential, changing behaviour of existing OTP tests
findings.body: Beyond the recovery codes needed for this PR, `getCredentials()` now also returns the stored OTP credential (and `updateCredential` assigns it a generated id). This makes the OTP credential visible through `SubjectCredentialManager.getFederatedCredentialsStream()` where previously nothing was returned, which can change what the account/admin credential endpoints list and which id the client receives — exactly what `testOTPSetupAndRemoveThroughAccountMgmtAndLogin` asserts (`assertEquals(1, otpCreds.size())` and deletion by that id expecting 204). This unrelated change should be dropped or its impact on the existing OTP tests verified.

findings.title: Unnecessary 'delayed-authenticator' execution in the test browser flow
findings.body: `configureBrowserFlowWithRecoveryAuthnCodes` adds a REQUIRED `delayed-authenticator` execution (with the config alias typo "delayed-suthenticator-config") to the copied browser flow, and the only call site passes `delay = 0`. The delay serves no purpose for this test while adding a hard dependency on an unrelated test-only authenticator provider: if `delayed-authenticator` is not deployed, flow creation/login in this test fails for reasons unrelated to recovery codes. Either drop the extra execution or explain/exercise the delay.
